calls.head: Calgary pounces on mistakes, and Seattle makes them
calls.body: Seattle gives up more dangerous chances after losing the puck than most (25th of 32 at avoiding breakdowns). Calgary ranks 9th for chances off turnovers.
calls.call: At least its usual 7.5% of Calgary’s 5-on-5 chances come right after winning the puck.

calls.happened: 15.5% of Calgary’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against its usual 7.5%.

calls.head: Sheltered against exposed
calls.body: On quality allowed, Seattle sits 2nd of 32, at the sheltered end of the scale. Calgary is 17th, at the exposed end.
calls.call: Seattle keeps the shots it allows further from danger than Calgary does.

surprises.head: Calgary leaned on its bottom six
surprises.body: Calgary’s bottom-six forwards played 47% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against its usual 42% and a league average of 42%. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: A rough night for D. Wolf
surprises.body: D. Wolf allowed 6 goals on shots worth 4.1 expected goals, 1.9 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 9 starts over the last three seasons.
